gm-void.purpose: Page background, and the ink colour on lime, gold or cyan fills.

gm-night.purpose: The one raised plane: panels, terminals, HUD, cartridges.

gm-deep.purpose: Title bars, inset strips, oversized decorative ticker type.

gm-line.purpose: The 2px border on every panel and its resting shadow.

gm-grape.purpose: Brand colour and the main branch. Drenches the stage-map section.

gm-grape-hi.purpose: Icons and graph strokes on dark surfaces. Never body text.

gm-grape-edge.purpose: Pressed edge under grape controls, locked tiles, dot texture.

gm-lime.purpose: Success, completion, and every primary call to action.

gm-cyan.purpose: Feature branches in commit graphs, and the global focus ring.

gm-cyan-edge.purpose: Pressed edge and dark-on-light pairing for cyan.

gm-coral.purpose: Fix branches, destructive Git output, error states.

gm-coral-edge.purpose: Pressed edge and dark-on-light pairing for coral.

gm-gold.purpose: Score, coins, rewards, the shop. Currency and nothing else.

gm-gold-edge.purpose: Pressed edge and dark-on-light pairing for gold.

gm-ink.purpose: Headings and primary text. 17.9:1 on void.

gm-ink-soft.purpose: Body copy. 12.2:1 on void, 5.5:1 on grape.

gm-ink-dim.purpose: Labels, terminal output, metadata. Void and night only.

display.purpose: The hero headline only, one per page. Bungee, positive tracking.

headline.purpose: Section titles and the closing call to action.

title.purpose: Stage names, feature titles, level-tile numerals.

body.purpose: All prose. Measure capped at 34rem / 52ch, text-wrap: pretty.

label.purpose: Quiet-button text, HUD labels, badges. Sentence case.

code.purpose: Anything Git itself would print: commands, hashes, branch names, HEAD.

shadows.name: control-rest
shadows.purpose: The solid edge below every arcade button (4px on the small variant).

shadows.name: control-hover
shadows.purpose: Paired with translateY(-2px): the button rises off its edge.

shadows.name: control-pressed
shadows.purpose: Paired with translateY(4px): the face sinks into the edge.

shadows.name: panel-rest
shadows.purpose: The HUD bar sitting on its own border colour.

shadows.name: sticker
shadows.purpose: Diagonal accent offset behind the hero terminal and feature cartridges. Blur is always 0.

motion.name: ease-out-expo

narrative.overview:
Git is the game world, and the interface is the cabinet it runs on. Branches are rails, commits are stations, HEAD is the player's token, and a merge is a level cleared. Every visual decision answers to that world: colour carries Git meaning, the display face is signage, and controls are physical buttons that sink when pressed. The surface is a dark violet night because the product is played, often in the evening, on a laptop next to an editor — not read like documentation under office light.

Loudness is earned, not sprayed. The hero, the stage select and the reward moments shout in saturated lime and grape; the surfaces people actually read stay calm and high-contrast. Chroma is carried by accents and typography, never by a gradient wash.

This system explicitly rejects the generic SaaS landing (purple gradients, glassmorphism cards, gradient headline text, three identical icon-feature tiles, hero-metric stat rows), the dry tutorial/docs look, kiddy edutainment, and the green-Matrix hacker cliché.
keyCharacteristics: Dark violet base, four saturated accents, each with a fixed Git meaning.
One display face (Bungee) for signage, Geist Sans for reading, Geist Mono for anything Git actually prints.
Hard, offset, zero-blur shadows. No glass, no soft glow, no gradient fills behind text.
Controls that visibly depress: a solid colour edge below the face that collapses on :active.
Motion is choreography, always with a static, complete prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
The landing page tokens are canonical; legacy purple-* routes migrate toward them.

rules.name: The Git Legend Rule
rules.body: Colour always means the same thing: grape = main, cyan = feature branch, coral = fix or danger, lime = commit succeeded, gold = points. A cyan button that isn't about branching, or a lime badge that isn't success, breaks the legend and is forbidden.

rules.name: The Grape Floor Rule
rules.body: On the grape surface, gm-ink-dim is prohibited (3.5:1). Text on grape is gm-ink or gm-ink-soft — nothing else. gm-ink-dim is for void and night only.

rules.name: The No Wash Rule
rules.body: Gradients never carry brand colour behind or inside text. The only permitted gradients are single-hue scrims over photography or video, whose job is contrast, not decoration. background-clip: text is banned outright.

rules.name: The Marquee-Only Rule
rules.body: Bungee is for headings, level numerals and the ticker. It never sets a sentence, never sets body copy, and never appears below 1.3rem except inside a button.

rules.name: The No Tracked Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Small uppercase letter-spaced kickers above section headings are prohibited. Where a marker is genuinely ordinal — the stage sequence — it is a plain two-digit mono number, not a styled label.

rules.name: The Overflow Test Rule
rules.body: Every display and headline string must be checked in German, Turkish and Hindi at 375px. If a word overflows, lower the clamp() minimum; don't let it bleed.

rules.name: The Zero-Blur Rule
rules.body: Every shadow in this system has a blur radius of 0 and an accent or line colour. Soft black shadows are permitted only inside an illustrative mock, never on real UI.

rules.name: The One Raised Plane Rule
rules.body: Content sits on void, and raised elements sit on night with a gm-line border. Never nest a raised surface inside another raised surface.

rules.name: The Theme Exception
rules.body: The terminal's purchasable themes (Dark Blue, Matrix, Golden) are the one place literal hex colours are allowed; they are sold goods with their own identity. The default theme is tokens only, and no other surface may follow their example.

rules.name: The Role Rule
rules.body: Inside the terminal every printed line picks a role (prompt, success, warning, error, accent, text) published by the frame as --term-* variables, never a token. A bought theme therefore repaints what the terminal says, not just its border.

dos: Do give every pressable control the edge treatment (0 5px 0 edge at rest, 0 1px 0 with a 4px translate on :active). Pressability is the system's signature.
Do keep the Git legend intact: grape main, cyan feature, coral fix/danger, lime success, gold points.
Do use gm-ink-soft for body copy on the grape section and gm-ink-dim only on void or night.
Do pair every state colour with an icon or text — check, padlock, HEAD — so colour is never the only signal.
Do ship every animation with a prefers-reduced-motion path that renders the finished state: no autoplaying video (poster only), no scroll-scrubbed lanes, no parallax.
Do render reveal animations on top of markup that is already complete in the HTML, so a headless renderer or a paused tab never ships a blank section.
Do use logical properties (ms-, me-, ps-, pe-, start-, end-) and rtl:rotate-180 on directional arrows; the product ships Persian.
Do test every heading in German, Turkish and Hindi at 375px before calling it done.
Do keep <video> backdrops muted, looping, playsInline, with preload="none" until playback is decided, and a poster that is the clip's own first frame.
Do style shared primitives once in src/components/ui/* and let screens inherit them; a screen only passes layout classes.
donts: Don't build a "generic SaaS landing": purple gradients, glassmorphism cards, gradient headline text, hero-metric stat rows, or three identical icon+heading+text tiles.
Don't let the page slide into the "dry tutorial / docs" look, or into kiddy edutainment that talks down to developers, or the green-Matrix hacker cliché.
Don't use background-clip: text, soft blurred shadows, backdrop-filter, or translucent glass on real UI.
Don't put a small uppercase letter-spaced eyebrow above a section heading, and don't number sections that aren't a real sequence.
Don't set body text in Bungee, and don't give it negative letter-spacing.
Don't put gm-ink-dim (3.5:1) or gm-grape-hi (4.2:1 on night) on body text.
Don't nest a gm-night surface inside another gm-night surface.
Don't wrap a <button> in a <Link> or hang onClick on a <div>; level tiles and CTAs are real buttons and links with real disabled states.
Don't remove a focus outline without replacing it with something at least as visible as the 3px cyan ring.
Don't extend the legacy purple-* Tailwind utilities on new work; add to the gm-* tokens or migrate the surface.
Don't colour a shared primitive at the call site; pick the variant, or add one.
Don't fade a disabled control to 50%; go flat (gm-deep + gm-ink-dim) so its label stays readable.
Don't write a bare z-50 or z-[999]; use the --z-* scale.
